posts.title: Privateer Frigate Fortuna LEGO 910059-1 (Stud.io Digital Recreation)
posts.text: Hello everyone! After spending some time away from digital LEGO building, I recently decided to give BrickLink Stud.io a try. In the past,I used to build quite a few digital models in LEGO Digital Designer (LDD), so it has been fun getting back into digital building with new software. For my first Stud.io project, I decided to recreate Privateer Fortuna, the beautiful ship designed by Brickperfection for the BrickLink Designer Program Series 7. This is a digital recreation of the original design, made for my own enjoyment and to explore the possibilities of Stud.io. All credit for the original design belongs to its creator. With the designer's blessing, I'm happy to share the Stud.io file with the Eurobricks community for anyone interested in taking a closer look at the model. Original BrickLink Designer Program project: BrickLink: Privateer Frigate Fortuna BDP Series 7 Digital model: Privateer Frigate Fortuna (Stud.io file) A big thank you to the original designer for creating such a fantastic model! I hope you enjoy exploring this epic build. A few notes about the digital model: Since I recreated this model before the official building instructions were available, I used a speed-build video as a reference to help complete the model. While I cannot guarantee that every single detail is identical to the original, I'm confident she is approximately 99% accurate. One small detail I couldn't get right in Stud.io is the attachment of the shrouds to their anchor points. Whenever I tried to attach them, Stud.io kept deleting them or moving them to completely different positions, so I eventually decided to leave them unattached in the digital model.

posts.text: The Venetian Houses set was very low volume and available five years ago. It's not LEGO designed. The Italian Riveria is really a very different style, albeit from the same country, but otherwise nothing in common. Venice is something different architecturally to what they've done before. posts.title: Adventurers on Holiday: a Short Story in Pictures
posts.text: Since spooky season is upon us, I thought it would be fun to do a little Halloween story featuring Johnny Thunder and company! "I say, Johnny," said Dr. Kilroy, "Taking a tour of the Peak District was a splendid idea. You've even managed to get Miss Reed to dress like a proper lady for a change." "You know I can hear you, right?" Pippin remarked. "A nice sightseeing trip is just what we need," said Johnny, unloading their luggage from the train and joining his friends on the platform. "No one shooting at us, no ancient curses, no scorpions. Just peace and quiet for once." "While we're in the area," said Dr. Kilroy, "There is an old Norman church nearby with an interesting inscription on one of the tombs that we-" "NO TOMBS!" Johnny and Pippin said in unison. While having dinner at a nearby pub, Johnny and company met Colonel Smythe, a local landholder. "So you're the famous Johnny Thunder," said the colonel. "Did you come here to investigate the strange goings-on of late?" "We're just on holiday," said Dr. Kilroy. "What strange goings-on?" Pippin asked, pulling out her notepad. "Some of the local farmers have had livestock turn up dead, drained of all their blood. My neighbour lost two of his sheep last night. Would you like to come with me to see them?" "I just wanted some peace and quiet," Johnny groaned. "I've never seen anything like it," said Johnny as he examined the bloodless sheep carcasses. "What could have done it?" Pippin asked, snapping pictures as fast as she could. "Have you ever heard of a fisi?" said Colonel Smythe. "Ah, from east African legend," said Dr. Kilroy. "A witch who takes the form of a hyena to feed on livestock. But of course that's just a myth." "It's as real as these dead sheep," the colonel exclaimed. "I encountered one in Kenya back in '98, and now there's one here in England." As night fell, Johnny and Colonel Smythe took up a position in the bushes to watch over the remaining sheep. "What the devil is that contraption?" Colonel Smythe whispered. "It's called a Thompson gun," Johnny replied, "And if I'd had one during the war I could have taken on a whole trench full of Huns by myself." "Newfangled nonsense," the colonel snorted. "I'll stick with my old Webley. I marched all over Africa with it and it never let me down. Why, once I-" "Sshhh!" Johnny hissed. "Something's coming!" To be continued...

posts.title: So, what Do people want?
posts.text: Here's my issue: I would love to get good at MOCing. I have visions, but not the skill to execute them. Just building the sets I buy doesn't seem to be teaching me much in the way of design principles, and just goofing around with parts doesn't help much either because I don't know how to teach myself. I can't seem to make the jump to where I can plan a build a few steps ahead as I'm building it. What I would love to see is some sort of "Master Builder Academy" line. A numbered series of sets in different sizes and complexities which are less about building specific models (though that would also be part of it) and more about learning the geometry of parts and practicing building techniques. Rather than step-by-step instructions for creating models, the instructions would be lessons in using that geometry and those techniques to create. And the lessons would be meant to be followed in sequence, starting with simple ideas like "3 plates to a brick" and overlapping pieces for stability and getting more advanced as you go. At the end of each lesson would be a "pop quiz" where you see a picture of a completed small model and the parts that go into it and are challenged to build it without step-by-step instructions. (If you get stuck, the answers are, of course, in the back of the book.) I would find that extremely helpful.

Im making a System moc while using Cada motors, and in a need of Buwizz version to post it online where Cada is not allowed. Maybe there is some mounting method requiring to change only a couple of pieces? Cada is basically two 2 by 3 bricks stacked on top of each other. It would be great if someone has both types of motors to compare.

posts.title: Lord of the Rings Ongoing Discussion
posts.text: Seems like Lego use a lot of old data for their decisions (however now with all the financial success they seem to take more chances lately), HP is a perfect example. They released a big wave that sold very well, then another one in a non movie year that bombed (this was in the start of the HP hype and Lego was almost bankrupt at the time so this was a big deal). In the coming years as the HP hype grew every year, Lego released fewer and fewer sets for every movie, then only 1 for the 5th film and stopped. I am sure those few sets sold a lot during that time, but Lego did not dare to take any chances. Then they made a few best of sets for the last 2 films and closed down the theme since they stopped making movies. For many years Lego as a rule never made sets for a licence without it having a big movie that year. Not a bulletproof strategy since new licenced films had to be a success, films like Prince of Persia Lone and ranger had great Lego set waves, but sold poorly because the films boombed. HP was the most asked for theme (they did not have) in Lego store for many years as the HP hype kept on growing as more people red the books and watch the films. So there was a clear demand, but Lego instead looked at data from 2002. Then the FB films came and finally Lego could take the chance and release sets again. In 2018 HP had 4 of the 10 bestselling products at Lego that year (no other theme had more than 1) and here we are 8 years later with it being a evergreen theme..

posts.title: (MOD) Umamusume: Pretty Derby Collectable Minifigures Series
posts.text: Despite having been around in Japan for around five years now (10 if you go all the way back to its initial announcement!), Umamusume: Pretty Derby has only recently blown up overseas thanks to the game's global launch last year. Essentially, Umamusume: Pretty Derby revolves around famous Japanese racehorses throughout history reimagined as anthropomorphized horse girls, competing in races based on real-life history. Beyond the mobile game, the franchise is also comprised of anime, manga, a feature-length film, and live concerts. I've become pretty obsessed in the series as of late and with its large and colorful cast of characters, I thought it would be great to make some Collectable Minifigures Series dedicated to this franchise and I eventually decided that I would try drawing every single playable character currently shown as a long-term project. This project began back in September of last year, and since then I've made four different series. I'll showcase each series in separate replies. Here is Series 1: 1. Special Week Accessories: Carrot piece with top, referencing one of her favorite foods Note: Special Week comes with a brand-new mold that combines both the skirt piece and the horse tail piece, which will be shared across multiple characters 2. Silence Suzuka Accessories: 2x1 printed tile of her good luck charm that she is gifted with in the anime 3. Tokai Teio Accessories: 1x1 cylinder brick + 1x1 round plate with pin representing her favorite drink 4. Daiwa Scarlet Accessories: A book containing the infamous SSR Kitasan Black card 5. Vodka Accessories: Two ball joints representing a basketball and a dodgeball, referencing two mini games from Umamusume: Pretty Derby - Party Dash 6. Mejiro McQueen Accessories: Teacup with saucer and a 2x2 printed tile of a newspaper showcasing her victory in the Spring Tenno Sho 7. Gold Ship Accessories: Book piece instead meant to represent a laptop showing the Pakatube channel 8. El Condor Pasa Accessories: S24 Falconer's falcon mold reprinted to represent El's pet bird Mambo 9. Taiki Shuttle Accessories: Pistol and 1x1 circular tile printed to resemble a coin, both referencing her ultimate animation 10. Haru Urara Accessories: Ice cream cone with two scoops referencing this SSR Guts card 11. Oguri Cap Accessories: Chopsticks, bowl with BB8's head representing a large serving of rice, and a plate with a build representing carrot hamburger steak. All of these represent Oguri's gluttonous nature. 12. Grass Wonder Accessories: Naginata (bar + lightsaber + a Ninjago blade piece) 13. Matikanefukukitaru Accessories: Crystal ball (1x1 round plate + minifigure head + Mysterio's fishbowl helmet mold) 14. Rice Shower Accessories: A blue flower referencing her ultimate animation 15. Sakura Bakushin O Accessories: Megaphone and 2x2 printed tile depicting a cover of her acclaimed song 16. Mihono Bourbon Accessories: Rabbit plush mold representing the one that she mentions owning 17. Agnes Tachyon Accessories: Flask mold and a potion build referencing this moment from an Umayuru episode 18. Symboli Rudolf Accessories: 2x3 printed tile showcasing Tracen Academy's school motto Here is the checklist: The packaging: And finally, here is a special baseplate that comes with this series in particular, recolored in bright green and printed with a horseshoe design: And that was Series 1! This was the first series I've drawn in years, so there were a few quirks that would eventually be ironed out in the future series (such as not showing the tails of these figures).

posts.title: Bounty Boat, Lego 6247: A Fresh Review
posts.text: Great write up on this set. Small sets like this provided easy ways to get more minifigures in a theme along with specialty parts. Not to mention, really helped to build out a world around the mid to larger sized sets. I have some nostalgia for this set as it was my second pirate set and amongst the first 5 or 6 Lego sets in general (besides a Basic building set and a few race cars). I received a copy of this set in my Easter basket after having gotten Rock Island Refuge the previous Christmas. I was excited to add 3 more minifigures and a boat to my burgeoning pirate collection. I will admit that I was a bit disappointed at the time that the guards were wearing red uniforms instead of blue. I was only just starting to get more into Lego, so I really didn't know that the Blue Imperials were being phased out for Red Imperials at the time (didn't start getting the Lego magazine or shop at home catalogs until around this time or later in the year). For now the blue and red coats had to team up against the pirates, neither got any reinforcements for many many years besides some Islanders and Imperial Armada. I may have colored some white stickers with blue marker and cut them out in the shape of the red and put it over them to give myself four blue coats instead a few times. Don't worry, the torsos are just fine for being over 30 years old and show no remnants of the stickers lol. I guess I was a little ahead of my time with all the custom stickers available now. The pirate minifigure that comes with Bounty Boat is probably one of my favorite pirate figures. Honestly, I think I like the color combination of legs, torso, and hat.

posts.title: modern North American diesel electric locomotive - heavy set 7939 MOD (unsure on real world prototype)
posts.text: This model was made when I was struck by a bolt of inspiration. I was looking at a older MOC when I found a way to give the locomotive from set 7939 a proper nose and a more North American-look. The model just one cab, a gangway door at the rear end, a single headlight and dual ditch lights, and a B-B 'four axle' wheel arrangement. (although I could make it a six axle unit if I wanted to - it's not too hard to swap it out with minimal adjustments) The dark bluish gray / black color scheme shown is also the only one that looked good out of the many others I tried. The rear of the locomotive. The vents up on top are supposed to have the turbine fan print on them, while the other exposed studs (on the side walls) are supposed to have the loco number and RR name on them. Even though I designed this engine, I have absolutely no idea if this engine looks like any real diesel locomotive class, so if anybody has any guesses, feel free to drop them in the comments! (I'm not good with more modern locos, especially diesels.) If it doesn't appear to look like anything specific, please let me know too! Thoughts?

Without Griffin knights, Sepent knight, Horse knights etc. there would be no castle BDP sets. They could replace official sets only if they included new prints and instructions. I would still prefer official sets though. For consistency, storytelling etc. I see BDP more for niche stuff and even there the lack of custom prints for torsos is a serious problem. The great themes for BDP are Wild West (lego does not want to do that for political or whatever reasons), sadly space (SW licence) or themes like Tiny World of Wonders by Jonas Kramm or those from Hanwas etc. But for the big themes like castle, trains etc. I much prefer official sets and I see this new model even damaging.

posts.title: 2026/27 Castle [wishlist/speculation﻿]
posts.text: I am happy with most of the BDP sets AND need official LEGO ones. BDP sets do things that official LEGO sets can't in terms of build and part usage as they cater to a niche audience not the general public that official LEGO sets do. Official LEGO sets give us unique figures, prints, colors, and moulds and often have an elegance to them that makes them a joy to build, not to mention sometimes extraordinarily returned designers working together to come up with cool things.

posts.title: Futuron collection completed and some other Space sets
posts.text: In truth, my MOC inspiration has been pretty low lately. I only mod things I feel could have done better or just annoy me big time (like the holes and unused space in the Battrax cabin, or the entire lack of a bottom cabin part on the Spy-Trak I). Sure, I'll share some real pics when I get all the parts in. I'm first managing my orders for other upgrade plans and a few other missing and damaged pieces from other sets I've recently bought. When it's all in, then I can finally start building! My windscreen is in okayish condition, it's probably hard to find a really good one for a decent price so I have accepted it as it is. Shame these have never been part of any other sets. In case you don't know, the steering mechanism unfortunately scratches over the quarter panel so if you plan on using that, I would recommend putting some protective material between that red 2x10 plate under the big dish and the window. Sadly my rack isn't in the best shape either, I may end up having to replace it.

posts.title: [MOC] 24-7 Towing Company
posts.text: Welcome to 24-7 Tow, a towing company located in Lego City: This modular MOC reuses set 60081 from 2015 as a display on the roof of the building. The first floor contains garages (one for a pickup truck and another for a towed vehicle) and a waiting room. The upstairs area contains an office in the back and a meeting space for those visiting: A large "24-7 Tow" sign displays above the roof, which can light up at night (at least in the Lego universe it can. The lights obviously are just for decoration). It isn't perfect nor is it my best work, but with some modification I believe it can fit well in a city layout. Let me know your thoughts below!

posts.title: LEGO Star Wars Set Discussion 2026 - READ FIRST POST!!!
posts.text: Of course. We all have been there before. It's always more or less based on your personal priorities occasionally taking over. Although it does make a difference to me whether you see this downtime coming and intend for it to happen or not, because that's by your own choice. In this case, it really isn't. I wanted to be hyped, to be excited, to look forward to what's to come with my genuinely preferred glass half full approach, but I currently can't. To don't be able to turn up, when you actually really want to, is quite a terrible feeling to be had. At least for me when it's this abrupt. Anyways, slowly but surely picking up on things again, so I start with something simple: what are your Lego Star Wars shopping plans for the rest of the year? I only intend to get the infamous 327th Battle Pack and the current Advent Calendar before they retire. And the aforementioned Gingerbread AT-AT for Christmas. That's basically it.
